newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Jan-Nov retail sales fall 5.0 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Jan-Nov retail sales fall 5.0 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian retail sales in the first 11 months of the year were a real five percent lower than a year earlier, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.
Soaring inflation and a fall in the lev were the reasons for the decline, a NSI official said.
BULGARIA RETAIL SALES JAN-NOV JAN-OCT JAN-NOV'95
Food sales decreased by a real seven percent year-on-year while non-food sales were a real three percent lower.
Retailers sold goods and services worth 111.4 billion levs at current prices in November, down a real 27 percent from the same 1995 month, the NSI said.
Cumulative consumer price inflation for the first 11 months was 223.6 percent. Inflation in the 12 months to November 1996 was 232 percent, NSI figures showed.
The lev fell to 360 per dollar at the end of November from around 69 a year earlier. It traded around 71 per dollar at the beginning of 1996. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
